_comment: the screens the simulator harness walks. both drivers (drive_idb.py and xcui/UITests/PlanRunner.swift) read this file.
points, not pixels (an iPhone 17 Pro is 402 x 874 points). dy > 0 moves the finger UP by dy points, which scrolls the content down the page.
launch        {args?: [..], waitFor: label, waitType?: 'tab'|'button', timeout?: s}  (re)launch the app and wait for a label
dismissAlerts {tap?: ['Allow','OK'], seconds?: s}   tap a system alert (the notification question) if one is up
expectAbsent  {label, seconds?, orRelaunchWith?: [..], waitFor?, waitType?}  if the label shows up, note it and optionally relaunch with arguments
shot          {name}          a screenshot plus an accessibility dump, named <name>.png and <name>.tree.*
drag          {dy, x?: 8, hold?: 0.8}  one slow finger drag starting in the left gutter (x=8), so it never lands on a switch
tap           {label, match?: 'exact'|'prefix'|'contains', type?: 'tab'|'button', scrollDy?: 300, maxScrolls?: 0, tabIndex?, tabCount?: 3, tabFromBottom?: 58}
a tab is found by its label where the driver can see the tab bar (xcuitest); idb's accessibility tree has no tab bar, so give tabIndex (0 = left) and it taps that slot
back          {}              the navigation bar's back button
wait for 'Focusmaxxing mobile' (the switches screen's title), not for the 'Switches' tab: both drivers can see the title, only xcuitest can see the tab.
